A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIND framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and added experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIND evaluations on ScienceQA, A-OKVQA, and M3CoT, including component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative reasoning cases.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds perturbation, model-transfer, cross-dataset, rationale-quality, loss-comparison, and controlled baseline experiments.

M1.justification: RAD generation, the two P2CL stages, and MCA retain their procedures and objectives. Applying MIND to Qwen backbones does not document a new method component. The Equation 7 correction aligns the formula with the negative-mining procedure already described in v1.

E1.justification: The three datasets remain, but v2 substantially expands evaluation scenarios: Table 9 tests six injected reasoning-error conditions, including five unseen types, and Table 10 adds M3CoT-to-ScienceQA transfer. These introduce interference and distribution-shift conditions beyond the original evaluations.

E2.justification: ScienceQA Table 1 adds VaLiK and MemVerse, each with two model variants. New analyses also include untuned Qwen controls and InfoNCE alternatives. The original benchmark comparator sets are otherwise retained.

E3.justification: Added protocols include randomly sampling 100 examples per dataset for perturbations, evaluating 7B–9B Qwen backbones and cross-dataset transfer, and scoring rationales with Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B across four dimensions. Table 14 controls visual encoders and caption generators. These supplement rather than replace the original T5 settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic interference robustness, backbone compatibility, cross-dataset generalization, quantitative rationale assessment, InfoNCE temperature comparisons, and matched visual/caption controls. Earlier component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, and qualitative cases remain; their appendix renumbering is not new analysis.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 newly discloses a fixed training seed of 42. This does not establish additional runs. Neither version reports multi-seed uncertainty estimates or significance tests for MIND.

E6.justification: Existing MIND benchmark scores and ablations remain unchanged, including 92.29% on ScienceQA and 57.38% for MINDbase on M3CoT. Tables 9–11 and 13–14 add substantial results, including Qwen-based M3CoT accuracies of 85.85–88.65% and matched-module advantages of 3.82–4.50 percentage points. These are new experimental results, not increases in the original scores.

T1.justification: Equation 7 corrects hard-negative selection: v1 incorrectly applies Top-k to positive similarities, whereas v2 uses negative similarities. This repairs the mathematical definition to match the existing prose. Other definitions and objectives remain unchanged; no new proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: RAD supplies diverse rationales, P2CL enables discrimination and correction, MCA aligns rationale representations, and MIND achieves strong benchmark performance. The shortened abstract and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning unseen-error robustness, transfer across backbones and datasets, the suitability of margin loss over InfoNCE, and gains beyond stronger visual modules. New Appendix D qualifies applicability through RAD preparation costs, VQA-focused validation, fine-grained perceptual failures, and dependence on original rationale quality.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the caption generator as frozen, clarifies RAD prompt placeholders, and documents generator and judge identities for added evaluations. It also explicitly advertises data and code at the existing project link. Original T5 hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the cited VaLiK and MemVerse works associated with the new ScienceQA comparisons. The prompt-based versus learning-based related-work organization and principal novelty positioning remain unchanged. Most bibliography edits concern citation style and venue formatting.

P1.justification: The abstract is condensed, grammar and affiliations are edited, and prompt templates move from Section 3.2 to Appendix A. Discussion and appendix headings are expanded and reorganized, but most existing prose and the main narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a different conference layout with running headers, revised front matter, and reformatted tables. Appendix prose changes to full-width layout, enlarging the retained ablation table and hyperparameter figure. Five new tables are added, while earlier qualitative figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Table 14 reduces an important confound in v1’s headline comparisons by matching visual encoders and caption generators while retaining 3.82–4.50-point advantages. New robustness and transfer experiments directly strengthen evidence for the framework’s central correction and generalization claims. Quantitative rationale assessment, the equation correction, and explicit limitations further improve the paper. Single-seed reporting and limited implementation detail for new experiments remain weaknesses, but the overall evidential improvement is substantial.
